name: Aktori
instructions: 1. In a mixing bowl, combine buckwheat flour and wheat flour in the required ratio.
2. Add milk and sugar/jaggery gradually to the flour mix to form a smooth, thick batter without lumps.
3. Heat a flat griddle (tawa) over medium heat and grease it with a little ghee.
4. Pour a ladleful of the batter onto the griddle and spread it slightly into a round shape.
5. Cook on both sides, adding a small amount of ghee around the edges until the pancake is firm and golden brown.
6. Serve hot, traditionally paired with honey or extra ghee.
description: Aktori is a festive dish originating from the Spiti Valley in Himachal Pradesh. It is a celebratory cake or pancake made primarily from buckwheat, which is a staple crop in the high-altitude regions of the state. It is traditionally prepared during local festivals and special occasions.
